text: The chemical formula of table salt is NaCl (sodium chloride), often written as Na⁺Cl⁻ or NaCl. It represents the ionic bond between a sodium atom (which loses one electron to become a positively charged Na⁺ ion) and a chlorine atom (which gains that electron to become a negatively charged Cl⁻ ion). The resulting compound, sodium chloride, is electrically neutral overall, with the sodium and chloride ions held together by strong electrostatic attractions in a giant ionic lattice structure (a "face-centered cubic" structure, meaning the crystal is built from alternating Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions
